title: Clock simulation step
statement: Let $K$ and $W$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be an input bit string, and let $c$ be a configuration of $W$ on $x$ whose state is $q$. Let $r$ be an output register, let $\tau$ be a tape content function with $\tau(z)=1$, and let $z$ be an integer; for any fixed contents and head positions of the other tapes, one step of the clock machine from the configuration encoding $c$, with clock state indicating that it is simulating $W$ in its decoding phase, equals the encoded configuration after one step of $W$: the simulated state is updated according to $W$'s transition, the clock cell at $z$ is changed to blank and its head moves to $z-1$, and the output is the one-bit value indicating whether the updated register is not exactly the register containing only $1$ if $W$'s transition halts, and is empty otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: input bit string $x$ and configuration $c$ of $W$ on $x$
arbitrary other-tape contents and head positions
